hero.title: The Shunga Dynasty: A Paradigm Shift
hero.description: A study of the Brahminical resurgence and the transition from central imperialism to regional power in post-Mauryan India.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: The transition from the decline of the Mauryan Empire to the establishment of Kanva rule.

cards.details: Pushyamitra Shunga assassinated the last Mauryan king, Brihadratha, during a military parade.
Reign of Pushyamitra Shunga, who performed two Ashvamedha sacrifices.
Death of Devabhuti (last Shunga king) and rise of the Kanvas.

items.title: P-A-V-A
items.decryption: Center of power was Pataliputra and Vidisha; known for Ashvamedha rites and Sanchi/Bharhut art.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing Shunga rule with a total anti-Buddhist purge; archaeological evidence at Sanchi/Bharhut shows Buddhist patronage continued.
Assuming the Shunga empire spanned the entire Mauryan territory; it was significantly smaller and fragmented.
Misattributing the start of the 'Gandhara School' to Shungas (It is a later Kushan-era development).

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Magadha (Pataliputra)
  • Vidisha emerged as a crucial western capital
  • Controlled parts of Punjab and central India

Personalities

  • Pushyamitra Shunga: Founder, anti-Yavana defender
  • Agnimitra: Hero of Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram
  • Patanjali: Prolific grammarian and contemporary
  • Political Dynamics:
    • Shift from centralized bureaucracy to feudal/decentralized structure.
    • Constant conflicts with Indo-Greeks (Demetrius/Menander).
  • Religious & Cultural Shift:
    • Brahminical resurgence: Revival of Vedic rituals (Ashvamedha).
    • Literature: Patanjali's 'Mahabhashya' (commentary on Panini).
    • Architecture: Refinement of Stupas (Bharhut and Sanchi railings).
